**Discpress 1.3.1 is for iPhone and iPad: it's now online at [powerbeef.github.io/discpress](https://powerbeef.github.io/discpress/), so you can use it in Safari and save results of any size.** The CHDs it makes are the same as 1.3.0's.

## Download

**[⬇ discpress.html](https://github.com/PowerBeef/discpress/releases/download/v1.3.1/discpress.html)** (about 2.9 MB). The whole app in one file that works offline. To update, download it and use it instead of your old copy.

**Or use it online: [powerbeef.github.io/discpress](https://powerbeef.github.io/discpress/)**, the same file, published with each release. Best on iPhone and iPad.

## On iPhone and iPad

- **Use it in Safari.** Safari can't open a local HTML file, and apps that can, such as Sitecase, can't save results over about 512 MB: most DVD, PSP and PS2 games. In Safari, results of any size download to Files → Downloads. Once opened, the online copy works offline, and Share → **Add to Home Screen** keeps it as an app.
- **Big results no longer close the app.** The share sheet loads the whole file into memory, so results over 512 MB now download instead of opening it.
- **Results survive a reload.** If iOS reloads the page before you save, finished results are listed under **From your last visit**, ready to save or delete. A conversion cut off by the reload says so.
- **Fewer threads** on iPhone (2) and iPad (4), to stay within iOS's memory limits.
- **Inside apps like Sitecase**, a tip points big games to the Safari copy, with a Copy link button.
- **Lockdown Mode** is named when it's why Discpress can't start.

## Fixes

- **PSP and other identified games no longer ask "DVD CHD or CD CHD?"** once the game is known: PSP games are always DVD CHDs, PlayStation and Saturn games CD CHDs. The choice moves into Options, with a line saying why, and a type you pick yourself stays picked.
- **A share sheet that fails falls back to a download.**

## Nothing leaves your device

The page's Content Security Policy forbids it any network connection, in the downloaded file and online alike. The online copy is the release file byte for byte: each release now lists its SHA-256 (`discpress.html.sha256`), so you can compare them.
